review: Doubt on line 9 decided wrongly: the plain words do not make the Saakat the subject. ਸਾਕਤ has no aunkar (unlike ਸਾਕਤੁ in line 1) and ਪਾਈਐ is impersonal or passive, so the Darpan's reading (love is not had from Saakats) is the one the grammar supports. It is applied in the fixes above.

issue: Line 9, ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਬੰਧਨ ਤੋੜਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ: ਸਤਿਗੁਰ as the vocative O True Guru (Darpan: ਹੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ, the review's fix) or as the agent, the True Guru breaks the bonds (Faridkot: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੋਣ ਨੇ).
our reading: O True Guru, those whose bonds you break, setting them apart, do not go into the womb again.
alternatives: Those whose bonds the True Guru has broken become detached and do not enter the womb again (Faridkot).
decided because: The agent form in this shabad is ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ with sihari (line 5, ਗੁਰਿ ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ); here ਸਤਿਗੁਰ has none, so the vocative the Darpan gives fits the grammar; the sense (the Guru frees them) is the same either way.

issue: Who is not accepted and who is driven out: the faults that go along (Darpan), or the people who go on without virtues, the vepir (without a guide).
our reading: Those who go on (without virtues) are not accepted; the command there is: beat them and drive out these who have no guide.
alternatives: Darpan: the faults that go with us find no honour; beat these unruly ones and drive them out of yourself now.
decided because: ਗਏ and ਮੰਨੀਅਨਿ (plural passive) read most simply of persons who have gone on; ਵੇਪੀਰ is a word for people without a pir (guide); the Faridkot Teeka and Santhya read it so.

issue: ਸਰਮੁ: effort (Sanskrit shram, the Darpan) or modesty (Persian sharm).
our reading: modesty (ਸ਼ਰਮ) the water
alternatives: effort, toil as the water (Darpan).
decided because: Santhya and the Faridkot Teeka read sharm, shame before wrong deeds; the line's list of virtues (karni, santokh, garibi) fits a moral quality; the grammar decides neither.

issue: ਰਖੁ: the imperative keep, or a noun, the guard (rakha) of the crop.
our reading: humble living the guard (of the crop)
alternatives: keep humility as your dress (imperative).
decided because: The line lists the parts of farming as nouns (seed, suhaga); the Darpan glosses ਰਖੁ as ਰਾਖਾ and the Faridkot reads guarding the crop.

issue: ਹਾਣੁ: waning (qualifying the life, Santhya) or the passing of each breath made the shop (Darpan).
our reading: Make your ever-waning life the shop.
alternatives: Darpan: make every passing breath of your life the earning, in the shop.
decided because: Santhya derives ਹਾਣੁ from Sanskrit haani, decline; it then qualifies ਆਰਜਾ simply, leaving the image of the shop whole.

issue: ਮੁਖਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਟਕਸਾਲਾ: your mouth (your word) is the mint, or (forms struck) in your supreme (mukhi) mint (Darpan).
our reading: your mouth (your word) is the mint that strikes them
alternatives: all forms are struck in your chief mint (Darpan, Faridkot).
decided because: ਮੁਖਿ beside ਤੇਰੈ reads as your mouth; Santhya takes it so, as the Lord's command that shapes all.

issue: ਸਾਕਤ ਪ੍ਰੇਮੁ ਨ ਪਾਈਐ: the Saakat does not find love, or love is not had from (the company of) Saakats (Darpan).
our reading: The Saakat does not find (the Lord's) love.
alternatives: Love (for the Lord) is not obtained from Saakats (Darpan); by loving the Guru-less the Lord is not found (Faridkot).
decided because: The plain words pair the Saakat, who does not find love, with the one who finds the Lord through love of the True Guru.

issue: Who is the giver of joy and sorrow: the Guru himself, or God, met through the Guru (Darpan).
our reading: one who meets the Guru, the giver of joy and sorrow, is merged in (the Lord's) praise
alternatives: one who meets the Guru meets the Lord who gives joy and sorrow (Darpan).
decided because: The words set ਸੁਖ ਦੁਖ ਦਾਤਾ beside ਗੁਰੁ with nothing between them; we add nothing.

issue: ਸੋਹੰ: so-ham, he am I (Faridkot and the earlier Granth meaning at 59.2), or ਸੋਹੈ, shines (Darpan).
our reading: Sohang (he am I); there is no division (between him and the soul).
alternatives: His light shines everywhere and there is no gap in his pervading (Darpan).
decided because: The spelling is ਸੋਹੰ, as at 59.2 where our meaning reads Sohang; ਭੇਦੁ ਨ ਕੋਈ follows it naturally; kept consistent with 59.2.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰੁ ਮਿਲਿਆ ਸੋਈ: the Guru met is that very Lord, or the one who meets the Guru (sees this) (Darpan), or through the Guru that Lord has been attained (Faridkot).
our reading: O Nanak, the Guru who has been met is that very One.
alternatives: As above.
decided because: ਗੁਰੁ (nominative) ਮਿਲਿਆ ਸੋਈ reads most simply as the Guru met being that same Supreme Lord just named.

issue: ਮਨੁ ਮਾਨਿਆ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਖਾਈ: my mind is won over by the Naam, the friend (Faridkot), or the one whose mind trusts (the Guru) takes the Naam as friend (Darpan).
our reading: My mind is won over by the Naam, my companion.
alternatives: Darpan, as above.
decided because: The Rahao goes on in the first person (I fall at the Guru's feet), so the mind is the speaker's own.

issue: ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਬਾਣੀ ਸਬਦਿ ਪਛਾਣੀ (line 10): ਪਛਾਣੀ with an implied agent (he recognised through the Shabad that in every age the Bani is the way) or agentless (the Bani has been recognised through the Shabad).
our reading: In every age the Bani has been recognised through the Shabad (the review's fix, matching the Punjabi ਪਛਾਣੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ).
alternatives: Darpan: through the Guru's Shabad he came to recognise that in every age the Guru's Bani is the means of union.
decided because: ਪਛਾਣੀ is a feminine past participle agreeing with ਬਾਣੀ; the passive keeps every word without supplying a clause the line does not have, and the next half-line (ਮਨਹਿ, his mind) still carries the stanza's subject.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਜਨ ਸਾਚੇ ਸਾਚੁ ਕਮਾਵਹਿ: ਸਾਚੇ as an adjective of ਜਨ, or as the oblique of ਸਾਚਾ (of the True One).
our reading: The Lord's servants are true; they practise Truth.
alternatives: Darpan: the servants practise the True One's lasting Name (ਸਾਚੇ = of the True One).
decided because: ਸਾਚੇ stands right after ਹਰਿ ਜਨ with no postposition and agrees with it in the plural; the plain reading, taken also by the Faridkot Teeka's sense and the published English, keeps every word.

issue: ਅਮਰੁ ਸਿਰਿ ਬਾਦਿਸਾਹਾ: whose command is over the kings' heads.
our reading: Those in whose hearts the Guru's wisdom shines: their command holds over the heads of kings.
alternatives: The Lord's command (writ) is over the heads of kings (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: The line continues the Gurmukh of stanza 3 and leads into line 13's plural ਕਰਹਿ; the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka both give the command to those Gurmukhs.

issue: ਸਬਦਿ ਸਵਾਰਣਹਾਰਾ: who adorns whom.
our reading: Steeped in the Naam of the One who adorns (lives) through the Shabad.
alternatives: He (the devotee) is embellished by the Shabad (Sant Singh Khalsa); he adorns others by teaching (Faridkot).
decided because: ਸਵਾਰਣਹਾਰਾ is an agent noun (the one who adorns); the Darpan's reading, with God as that agent, fits the agent noun and the shabad's theme of the Lord's grace.

issue: ਸਦਾ ਰਹਹੁ ਸਰਣਾਈ: whose refuge, and the subject of line 6.
our reading: Remain in the Guru's refuge; he casts his glance, keeps your honour and grants the glory of the Lord's Name.
alternatives: The Lord's refuge, the Lord bestowing his own Name (Faridkot, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: Stanza 1 turns wholly on the True Guru as the way to devotion, and ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੋ ਦੇ (gives the Lord's Name) reads naturally of the Guru as giver; the Darpan reads so.

issue: ਸੋ ਗੁਰੂ ਸੋ ਸਿਖੁ ਹੈ: two predicates or one.
our reading: He is the Guru, and he the Sikh, whose light merges in the Light.
alternatives: Darpan: that one is the Guru's true Sikh.
decided because: The words give two parallel predicates (ਸੋ ਗੁਰੂ, ਸੋ ਸਿਖੁ); the Faridkot Teeka reads them so, and the sense (Guru and Sikh one in the Light) is the line's own.

issue: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਪਾਏ ਹਰਿ ਥਾਇ: the Gurmukh finds a place with the Lord, or the Lord accepts the Gurmukh (ਥਾਇ ਪਾਉਣਾ).
our reading: The Gurmukh finds a place in the Lord's presence.
alternatives: The Lord accepts the Gurmukh; the Lord places the Gurmukhs in his own abode (Faridkot).
decided because: ਹਰਿ stands between ਪਾਏ and ਥਾਇ, binding ਹਰਿ ਥਾਇ together (the Darpan's gloss: in the Lord's presence); both readings carry the same approval.

issue: ਨਿਰਮਲ ਬਾਣੀ: the means (through the pure Bani) or a third pure thing (his speech is pure).
our reading: Body and mind are pure through the pure Bani.
alternatives: Body, mind and speech become pure (Sant Singh Khalsa, Faridkot).
decided because: ਨਿਰਮਲੁ (singular, aunkar) agrees with ਤਨੁ ਮਨੁ and closes that clause; ਨਿਰਮਲ ਬਾਣੀ reads as the Bani that purifies, as the Darpan takes it, the Bani of the shabad's first line.

review: Line 4: the writer's conjunct-participle reading should be reversed. ਪਾਇਆ being perfect does not rule out the imperative: the Darpan keeps both (meditate; whoever did found peace), which is the reading the vocative needs. Fixed in pa and en.

issue: ਮੁਹਾਹੁ
our reading: from the mouth: he himself speaks with the mouth, from every mouth
alternatives: Darpan: a charming, sweet word spoken by God; Faridkot: he himself is the mouth, or is charmed
decided because: -ਾਹੁ is the ablative ending (ਧੁਰਾਹੁ, ਘਰਾਹੁ) and the verse rhymes on it; Faridkot and Manmohan Singh read the mouth

issue: ਸਿਰਿ
our reading: each one (ਸਿਰਿ ਸਿਰਿ): he sets each one to his task
alternatives: ਸਿਰਿ as having created (ਸਿਰਜ ਕੇ), our word meaning's example
decided because: Darpan and Santhya both read each one; ਉਪਾਇਦਾ already says he creates

issue: subject of ਮਿਲਾਹੁ: imperative or third person
our reading: third person: O servant Nanak, he in his grace unites (beings)
alternatives: imperative: forgive servant Nanak and unite him
decided because: every rhyme in -ਾਹੁ in this shabad (ਲਾਹੁ, ਜਾਹੁ, ਲੰਘਾਹੁ, ਚਲਾਹੁ) is third-person present; Darpan, Santhya the same

issue: who drips the Amrit into the mouth
our reading: the True Guru, in whom the treasure is
alternatives: Santhya: the Beloved Lord, in mercy, drips it
decided because: the treasure is said to be in the Guru; Darpan, Faridkot and the published translations read the Guru

issue: ਆਪੇ ਕੀਮਤਿ ਪਾਇਦਾ: whose worth
our reading: his own worth (only he can value himself)
alternatives: the worth of all beings (as Darpan reads the same words in 606.1)
decided because: Darpan and Santhya read his own worth here; in 606.1 the next words, the scales and the weight, point to his valuing of beings, so that line reads the worth of all

issue: who is sated: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ subject or vocative
our reading: vocative: O servant Nanak, the Beloved (himself) is sated with the Lord's relish
alternatives: servant Nanak is sated with the Lord's relish (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa)
decided because: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ has no aunkar (vocative form), and the whole stanza says the Beloved himself is the Amrit and its relish; Darpan and Faridkot the same

issue: ਤੀਰਥੁ
our reading: the tirath as a crossing place (ford), with the raft
alternatives: a place of pilgrimage (Faridkot, SSK)
decided because: the line is about crossing over with a raft; Darpan reads the river bank; a note gives both senses

issue: ਧਿਆਇ … ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ
our reading: conjunct participle: meditating on the Lord, (one) has found peace
alternatives: imperative: meditate, and you will find peace (Faridkot)
decided because: ਪਾਇਆ is perfect, not future; Darpan joins both (meditate; whoever did found peace), our reading keeps the perfect

issue: ਬੰਨਿ ਬਕਰੀ ਸੀਹੁ ਹਢਾਇਆ
our reading: God, having tied the lion to the goat, leads it about (his fear keeps the mighty with the weak)
alternatives: Darpan: the goat leads the tied lion about; SSK: he binds the tiger and the goat together
decided because: ਹਢਾਇਆ is causative with God as agent, as ਰਖਾਇਆ and ਲਵਾਇਆ in the same shabad

issue: ਵਡਭਾਗੀ and ਲੈ
our reading: the fortunate one has bliss night and day; ਲੈ imperative: earn the Lord's profit
alternatives: Faridkot: O fortunate one (vocative), you will have bliss
decided because: Darpan's reading; ਲੈ is an imperative addressed to the mind of the Rahao

issue: ਕੇਸੁ
our reading: Keshi, the demon (a list of names, all with aunkar)
alternatives: Faridkot: Kans seized by the hair (ਕੇਸ)
decided because: the three nouns stand together as objects of ਮਾਰਾਹਾ; our 224.2 reads ਕੰਸੁ ਕੇਸੁ ਚਾਂਡੂਰੁ as Kans, Keshi and Chandur

issue: ਜਪਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਭਗਤਿ ਸਮਾਹਾ
our reading: O Nanak, repeating (the Name), one merges in devotion
alternatives: Darpan: imperative, repeat and stay absorbed; SSK: Nanak is absorbed
decided because: ਸਮਾਹਾ is third-person present like the other rhymes in -ਾਹਾ; ਜਪਿ a conjunct participle

issue: ਨਾਨਕ … ਪਾਇਆ: subject
our reading: O Nanak, (such a one) has found the peace of Sahaj
alternatives: Nanak has found the peace (SSK)
decided because: the line continues the last one (those on whom grace has fallen) and ਜਾਗਤੁ ਰਹੈ is third person; Darpan the same

issue: ਦੀਨ ਦਇਆਲ ਭਏ ਹੈ
our reading: the Lord, merciful to the meek, has become kind (to such a one), whose thirst is quenched
alternatives: the Lord has become merciful to meek Nanak (SSK)
decided because: ਦੀਨ ਦਇਆਲ is the epithet of God, with honorific ਭਏ ਹੈ; Darpan the same

issue: ਅਵਰੁ ਨ ਕੋਈ
our reading: there is no other giver
alternatives: no one else can receive it without your gift (Darpan)
decided because: both come to the same; the line contrasts the Giver with all others

review: Decision on the subject of ਨਹ ਬਿਸਰੈ is not borne out by the grammar: the verb is third person, so not Madhav addressed (ਦੇਹੁ, 2nd person); the nearest antecedent is ਓਟ ਚਰਨਾ.
reviewer_fix: our reading: (the shelter of the Guru's feet) is never forgotten, as the Darpan (and the Faridkot's ਏਹੁ ਭਾਵਨਾ) read it.

review: The SSK/MM reading the writer took fails gender agreement (ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ fem., ਪਿਆਰਾ masc.).
reviewer_fix: our reading: he keeps his servants close with his own love and affection (Darpan); Faridkot's 'the lover of his own love' also keeps ਪਿਆਰਾ masculine.

issue: subject of ਨਹ ਬਿਸਰੈ (line 4); the writer's doubts file still gives (you, Madhav)
our reading: (the shelter of the Guru's feet) is never forgotten, as the review's fix has it
alternatives: writer: (you, Madhav) never slip from my mind; SSK: not forget the saints
decided because: ਬਿਸਰੈ is third person while Madhav is addressed in the second (ਦੇਹੁ); the Darpan reads (ਇਹ ਆਸਰਾ) ਮੈਨੂੰ ... ਨਾਹ ਭੁੱਲੇ; the review's fix stands

issue: ਅਪੁਨੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਪਿਆਰਾ (line 8); the writer's doubts file still gives love for him is dear to him
our reading: he keeps his servants close in his own love and affection, as the review's fix has it
alternatives: writer, SSK/MM: love for him is dear to him; Faridkot: the lover of his own love
decided because: feminine ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ cannot take masculine ਪਿਆਰਾ as predicate; the Darpan: ਆਪਣੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਦੀ ਆਪਣੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਦੀ ਦਾਤਿ ਦੇ ਕੇ; the review's fix stands

issue: ਗੁਰੁ ਗੋਵਿੰਦੁ: two nominatives
our reading: the Guru, Govind (apposition), as 234.2 renders ਗੁਰ ਗੋਵਿੰਦੁ
alternatives: Darpan: the greatest Govind (ਗੁਰੁ = great); SSK: the Guru and the Lord
decided because: consistency with our earlier rendering; both words in aunkar stand in apposition

issue: ਵਡਭਾਗੀ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਾਇਆ … ਧਿਆਇ
our reading: the fortunate one who has found the Guru meditates (ਧਿਆਇ = ਧਿਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ)
alternatives: SSK/MM: by good fortune I found the Guru and I meditate
decided because: Darpan's ਪਦਅਰਥ; the stanza speaks generally of seekers

issue: ਨਿਰਮਲ ਸਾਚੇ ਸੋਇ
our reading: pure is the praise (ਸੋਇ) of the True One
alternatives: SSK/MM: those who are true are pure; Faridkot: those who repeat him become pure and glorious
decided because: ਸਾਚੇ oblique genitive with feminine ਸੋਇ (ਸੋਭਾ); line 16 then speaks of receiving it

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਰਤਾ ਸਚਿ ਨਾਮਿ
our reading: O Nanak, (such a one, the rare servant of line 17) is imbued with the True Name
alternatives: SSK/MM: Nanak is imbued with the True Name
decided because: continuity with line 17's ਜਨੁ; Darpan reads so

issue: subject of ਨਹ ਬਿਸਰੈ
our reading: (you, Madhav) never slip from my mind
alternatives: Darpan: (this shelter) is not forgotten; SSK: not forget them (the saints)
decided because: the prayer is addressed to Madhav; the third person ਬਿਸਰੈ fits God not being forgotten

issue: ਤੀਨਿ ਸੰਙਿਆ ਕਰਿ ਦੇਹੀ ਕੀਨੀ ਜਲ ਕੂਕਰ ਭਸਮੇਹੀ
our reading: the body is made with three ends fixed: water, dogs or ashes
alternatives: Darpan: body made under the three gunas, ending in water, dogs or dust; Faridkot gives both
decided because: ਸੰਙਿਆ = designation, and the line itself lists the three (Faridkot, SSK, MM read so); note added

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧਾਰੀ … ਗਹੇਹੀ
our reading: past: God has shown mercy to servant Nanak; I have grasped the True Guru's shelter
alternatives: Darpan: prayer, O God, show mercy, that I hold the Guru's shelter
decided because: ਧਾਰੀ is feminine past agreeing with ਕਿਰਪਾ; Faridkot, SSK, MM read past

issue: ਕੋਇ ਨ ਪਹੁਚਨਹਾਰਾ ਦੂਜਾ
our reading: no other can equal (the Master)
alternatives: SSK/MM: no one can equal me; Faridkot: no one can reach (harm) me
decided because: read with the half-line on the Master's support, as the Darpan does

issue: ਅਪੁਨੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਪਿਆਰਾ
our reading: love for him is dear to him
alternatives: Darpan: he gives them the gift of his love; Faridkot: he is the lover of his own love
decided because: SSK/MM and Faridkot agree on the sense that devotion to him is dear to him; closest to the words

issue: whose greatness and glory
our reading: his (God's), continuing lines 7–8
alternatives: Darpan: the Guru's
decided because: the subject of the preceding stanza is God

issue: addressee of ਲੇਹੁ ਨਿਬਾਹੀ
our reading: (O Sants)
alternatives: SSK/MM: O Lord
decided because: the stanza is about taking the Sants' shelter; Darpan and Faridkot address the Sants

issue: ਨਿੰਦਉ ਨਾਹੀ
our reading: I speak ill of nothing (first person)
alternatives: SSK: do not slander (command)
decided because: the -ਉ ending is first person singular (Darpan: ਮੈਂ ਨਿੰਦਦਾ)

issue: ਗੁਰ ਨਾਨਕ ਕੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ
our reading: O Nanak, the Guru's greatness
alternatives: SSK/MM: the greatness of Guru Nanak
decided because: style §12: ਗੁਰ goes with the words around it, ਨਾਨਕ is the signature; Darpan reads so

issue: ਤੂ ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰ ਹਾਈ
our reading: you are my brother through the Guru (ਗੁਰ ਹਾਈ = ਗੁਰਭਾਈ)
alternatives: Shabdarth: ਹਾਈ is Lahndi 'are', you are my Guru; SSK: You are our Guru
decided because: ਗੁਰ without aunkar is not a nominative; the line's children-of-one-father image and the address ਮੀਤਾ fit a fellow disciple; Darpan and Faridkot read so

issue: trailing ਰੇ at line ends
our reading: left unrendered (an exclamatory particle)
alternatives: Darpan renders it ਹੇ ਭਾਈ
decided because: as our earlier meanings treat line-final ਰੇ (156.1)

issue: ਸੁਖਮਨ ਨਾਰੀ
our reading: the Sukhmana channel (yogic figure), as 327.1 renders it
alternatives: Darpan: the senses (ਨਾਰੀ) become givers of peace to the mind
decided because: the Shabdarth and our glossary give ਸੁਖਮਨਾ ਨਾੜੀ; note added

issue: ਰਾਖੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੇ
our reading: the fiends plead: save us from (your) Master
alternatives: read ਠਾਕੁਰ as vocative: save us, O Master
decided because: Darpan, Faridkot, Shabdarth and SSK all read ਤੇ as 'from'

issue: ਗੁਰਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਕਉ
our reading: the Guru (ਗੁਰਿ, instrumental) entrusted (them) to Nanak
alternatives: SSK: the Lord blessed Guru Nanak
decided because: sihari on ਗੁਰਿ marks the agent; ਨਾਨਕ ਕਉ is the receiver

review: Doubt on line 5 (ਭਾਈ) decided the wrong way: in this shabad the addressee is ਪਿਆਰੇ (God), and the Darpan and Faridkot both take ਭਾਈ as ਪ੍ਰੇਮੀ; the identical line in 611.3 is a vocative there because a friend (ਮੀਤਾ) is addressed. Fixed in pa/en line 5. The other twelve doubts: the writer's decisions are borne out by the grammar and context (612.3:10, 613.1:10, 613.3:5, 613.3:9, 614.2:9, 614.3:10, 615.1:6, 615.2:7, 615.2:9, 615.2:10, 615.3:9, 616.2:7).
reviewer_fix: Read ਭਾਈ = ਪ੍ਰੇਮੀ: this mind has become your lover.

issue: ਇਹੁ ਮਨੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਭਾਈ is the same line as 611.3 (batch 04), which renders it 'O brother, this mind is yours'; repeated lines are normally rendered alike.
our reading: Here: this mind has become your lover (ਭਾਈ = ਪ੍ਰੇਮੀ), addressed to God (ਪਿਆਰੇ, line 1).
alternatives: Render it as in 611.3, a vocative 'O brother'.
decided because: The context differs: 611.3 addresses a friend (ਸੁਣਿ ਮੀਤਾ) and offers the mind to him, while 614.1 addresses ਪਿਆਰੇ, glossed by the Darpan as ਹੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, and no brother is addressed; the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read ਭਾਈ = ਪ੍ਰੇਮੀ here. The two renderings differ deliberately; this is not a refrain inconsistency.

issue: Who takes the Sants' shelter: Nanak himself, or those of whom the line tells (ਭਏ is plural).
our reading: O Nanak, (those who) have taken hold of the shelter of the Sants are absorbed in (the Lord's) feet.
alternatives: Nanak has grasped the Sants' shelter and his heart is absorbed in the Lord's feet (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: ਭਏ is plural and the stanza speaks of classes of people throughout; the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read it so.

issue: Nanak as the one who thirsts, or a vocative with an implied third person.
our reading: Nanak thirsted for the sight (of the Lord), and God, the Knower of hearts, has met (him).
alternatives: O Nanak, (whoever) thirsts for the sight, God comes to meet him (Darpan).
decided because: ਲਗੀ and ਮਿਲਿਆ are past and particular; the Faridkot Teeka reads it of the Guru himself; Nanak speaking of himself takes the subject (style §12).

issue: Who was joined to the Saadh Sangat and heard the Word: the speaker or anyone.
our reading: When you yourself brought (me) into the Saadh Sangat, then I heard your Word; line 10 Nanak is in bliss.
alternatives: Whenever you join someone to the Saadh Sangat, he hears your praise (Darpan).
decided because: ਮਿਲਾਇਓ, ਸੁਨੀ are past; the Faridkot Teeka reads mere ko; the closing line is Nanak's own bliss.

issue: ਭਾਈ: vocative (O brother) or a predicate noun, the lover (Darpan: this mind is now your lover).
our reading: O brother, this mind is yours.
alternatives: This mind has become your lover, O Lord (Darpan, Faridkot); O Sants, my brothers, this soul is yours (Manmohan Singh).
decided because: ਭਾਈ is overwhelmingly vocative in the Granth, and the same Rahao line in the earlier Sorath shabad (ਸੁਣਿ ਮੀਤਾ ਧੂਰੀ ਕਉ ਬਲਿ ਜਾਈ ॥ ਇਹੁ ਮਨੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਭਾਈ ॥) is followed by ਇਹੁ ਮਨੁ ਤੈ ਕੂ ਦੇਸਾ (611.3), offering the mind to the friend addressed; the plain reading of the words is kept.

issue: The list of names: vocative, or the names whose Naam line 10 speaks of.
our reading: Gobind, Damodar, the merciful Madhav, the Supreme Lord, the Formless One: (his) Name is (my) everyday provision ...
alternatives: A vocative address (Faridkot); a command to make the Naam one's daily goods (Darpan).
decided because: Line 10 has no verb of command; it is a statement of what the Naam is, and the names identify whose Name.

issue: ਪੂਰ ਕਰੰਮਾ: perfect destiny or works fulfilled.
our reading: all his works come to fruition
alternatives: his karma (destiny) is perfect (Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: The Darpan glosses ਕਰੰਮਾ as ਕੰਮ, and the shabad has just said ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਾਮਾ (line 6).

issue: ਕਤ ਆਵੈ ਕਤ ਜਾਈ: of God, or of the person who has drunk the Name.
our reading: The Supreme God is present everywhere: from where would he come, and to where would he go?
alternatives: That person no longer comes and goes in births (Darpan).
decided because: The line's own subject is ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ; no new subject is named; Manmohan Singh and Sant Singh Khalsa read it so.

issue: Whom all praise, and to whom the Sangat is dear.
our reading: Everyone hails and praises (me); dear (to me) is the company of the Saadh.
alternatives: Everyone praises the one to whom the Guru's company is dear (Darpan).
decided because: Line 8 is first person, the Rahao is the Guru's own (ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਆ ਆਪਿ ਸਹਾਈ), and the Faridkot Teeka reads hamari.

issue: ਗੋਸਟਿ: discourse, or union (Darpan: ਮਿਲਾਪ).
our reading: hearing the discourse (of God), the wisdom and the Naam
alternatives: they obtained union with God and wisdom, and were saved by hearing the Name (Darpan).
decided because: ਗੋਸਟਿ, ਗਿਆਨੁ, ਨਾਮੁ stand together as objects of ਸੁਣਿ; the Faridkot Teeka and Manmohan Singh take it as discourse.

issue: Who came home: Nanak, or whoever God is merciful to.
our reading: Nanak's own God has become merciful (to him), and he has come home in bliss.
alternatives: O Nanak, the one on whom God is merciful merges in bliss in the Lord's feet (Darpan).
decided because: The verbs are past and particular and the shabad is in the first person; the Faridkot Teeka reads it of the Guru's own return home.

issue: ਕਰਿ ਸੇਵਾ ਸੇਵਕ: a command, and ਸੇਵਕ as manner or vocative.
our reading: Serve your own God as his servant, (the One) who has fulfilled the wish of your mind.
alternatives: God fulfils the wishes of the servants who serve him (Faridkot).
decided because: ਕਰਿ is the imperative singular; the Darpan glosses ਸੇਵਕ as ਸੇਵਕਾਂ ਵਾਂਗ.

issue: Subject of ਸੰਮਾਨੈ, ਜਾਨੈ: man in general or we.
our reading: (Man) counts the made thing as great as Mount Meru ...
alternatives: We creatures count ... (Faridkot).
decided because: The verbs are third person singular.

issue: Whose mind is attached to the Guru's feet.
our reading: The mind is attached to the Guru's feet ... (subject left as the line has it).
alternatives: my mind (Sant Singh Khalsa); the mind of whoever (Darpan).
decided because: The line names no owner; line 10 ends on Nanak, so a first-person sense is open but not added.

review: The decision stands, but the record is incomplete: the Darpan's own meaning takes ਭਾਈ as addressed to God (ਹੇ ਭਾਈ! ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ!; ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ! ਮੈਨੂੰ ਬਚਾ ਲੈ), and the Faridkot Teeka, like the Shabdarth, reads my dear ones or Hargobind as the object.
reviewer_fix: Plain grammar: ਰਾਖਿ ਲੈਹੁ is the prayer, ਮੇਰੇ ਕਉ its object (me), ਭਾਈ a vocative, as everywhere in this run (619.2, 620.3); the Darpan agrees on ਮੇਰੇ ਕਉ = me but turns ਭਾਈ to God. Reading ਭਾਈ ਮੇਰੇ ਕਉ as my dear one, the child (Shabdarth, Faridkot) gives ਭਾਈ an unusual sense and puts a person in the line who is not named; so not taken.

issue: ਸੁਣਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਕੀ ਅਰਦਾਸਾ (line 6): conjunct participle or present tense?
our reading: Conjunct: hearing Nanak's prayer, the True Master has forgiven all.
alternatives: Darpan glosses ਸੁਣਿ as ਸੁਣੈ: the True Master, who has forgiven all, hears Nanak's prayer too.
decided because: Sihari on the verb stem is the regular conjunct participle, and it gives the line one plain clause; the Darpan's ਸੁਣੈ needs an implied relative. Not changed.

issue: ਰਾਖਿ ਲੈਹੁ ਭਾਈ ਮੇਰੇ ਕਉ: whom is the prayer for?
our reading: ਭਾਈ is a vocative (O brother) and ਮੇਰੇ ਕਉ is me: Save me: this, O brother, is my prayer before God.
alternatives: The Shabdarth reads ਭਾਈ ਮੇਰੇ ਕਉ as my dear one, the child Hargobind: Save my dear one.
decided because: The Darpan's grammar gives ਭਾਈ as a vocative and ਮੇਰੇ ਕਉ as me; ਭਾਈ is a vocative throughout this run of shabads (619.2, 620.3).

issue: ਪਛਾਣਿ and ਮਾਣਿ (lines 1–2): imperative, conjunct participle, or present tense?
our reading: Present tense, as ਪਛਾਣੈ, ਮਾਣੈ: God keeps in view his innate way; his servant enjoys his love for ever.
alternatives: ਮਾਣਿ as an imperative (enjoy his love for ever); ਪਛਾਣਿ as recognising (conjunct).
decided because: The Darpan glosses both as present tense (ਪਛਾਣੈ, ਮਾਣੈ), and the stanza is a statement about God's way, not a command.

issue: ਧਿਆਈ, ਵਿਸਰਉ ਨਾਹੀ, ਪਾਈ: statement or wish?
our reading: Wishes: may I meditate; may God never be forgotten; may I obtain.
alternatives: Statements: I meditate, I do not forget, I obtain.
decided because: The Darpan reads ਵਿਸਰਉ as the optative third person (ਹੁਕਮੀ ਭਵਿੱਖਤ) and ਧਿਆਈ, ਪਾਈ as first-person wishes; the address to the Sants is a request.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰ: O Guru Nanak, or Nanak addressing the Guru?
our reading: Says Nanak, O Guru, your word is unshakeable.
alternatives: O Guru Nanak, your word is unshakeable (the Fifth Guru addressing Guru Nanak).
decided because: The Darpan glosses ਨਾਨਕ and ਗੁਰ as two vocatives (ਹੇ ਨਾਨਕ! ਹੇ ਗੁਰੂ!); style.md §12 keeps ਨਾਨਕ as the signature and puts ਗੁਰ with the words around it.

issue: Spelling of ਹਰਿ ਗੋਵਿਦੁ (also 620.5), a person's name.
our reading: Hargobind / ਹਰਿਗੋਬਿੰਦ, as our 500.5 renders the same person.
alternatives: Hargovind / ਹਰਿਗੋਵਿੰਦ, following the line's spelling (the rule for God's names Gobind/Govind).
decided because: This is the name of one person, (Guru) Hargobind, already written Hargobind / ਹਰਿਗੋਬਿੰਦ in the Granth's meanings (500.5); one person keeps one spelling.

issue: ਥਾਤੀ ਅਗਮ ਅਪਾਰ: sense of ਥਾਤੀ.
our reading: the lasting store (of the wealth of the Naam) of the unreachable, infinite Lord.
alternatives: Darpan: ਥਾਤੀ from sthiti, abode: where this wealth is gathered, the unreachable Lord abides. Shabdarth: a boundless, peerless store of wealth.
decided because: Both senses, store and lasting abode, are in the word; the line is about the wealth gathered, so the store that lasts keeps both without adding a clause the line does not have.

issue: ਜਗਤ ਜੀਵਨੁ: the world (subject) and life (object), or the Life of the world?
our reading: O God, forgetting you, how can (anyone) attain the Life of the world?
alternatives: How can the world find life, forgetting you?
decided because: The Darpan glosses ਜਗਤ ਜੀਵਨੁ as one phrase, the Life of the world (God); ਪਾਵੈ has no other object.

review: The doubt record misstates the Faridkot Teeka. It reads the Guru (honorific ਹੋਏ) as kind to our whole family, as the Darpan does, so only the Shabdarth reads all became kind to us. The meaning can stand: ਗੁਰਿ ਪੂਰੈ in the same line is a singular agent, so ਹੋਏ more naturally takes ਸਰਬ as its subject, as the parallels 618 (ਸਭ ਘਟ ਉਪਜੀ ਦਇਆ) and 622.1 (ਸਭਿ ਜੀਅ ਭਏ ਦਇਆਲਾ, ਸਭ ਉਠਿ ਲਾਗੀ ਪਾਈ) bear out. The record should give the grounds correctly.

issue: ਹੋਏ ਸਰਬ ਦਇਆਲ: who is merciful to whom
our reading: all have become kind (to me)
alternatives: the Darpan: the Guru is ever kind to all beings
decided because: ਹੋਏ is plural and ਸਰਬ is its subject; the Faridkot Teeka and the Shabdarth read all became kind to us (the Shabdarth points to 618's ਸਭ ਘਟ ਉਪਜੀ ਦਇਆ).

issue: ਸਭਿ ਜੀਅ ਭਏ ਦਇਆਲਾ
our reading: all beings have become kind (to me)
alternatives: the Darpan: you are kind to all beings
decided because: ਸਭਿ ਜੀਅ is a nominative plural with the plural ਭਏ; read as in 621.1, as the Shabdarth does.

issue: ਰਖਵਾਲੇ ਗੁਰ ਗੋਪਾਲਾ: ਗੁਰ as Guru or great
our reading: O Guru, O Gopal, you are (my) protector
alternatives: the Darpan's prose: O greatest one, O Sustainer, O Protector (three vocatives)
decided because: the Darpan's own word gloss is ਗੁਰ — ਹੇ ਗੁਰੂ; the Faridkot Teeka reads ਰਖਵਾਲੇ as the predicate (you, as the Guru, are our protector), which fits the following lines.

issue: Who is speaking and in what tense (lines 2-11)
our reading: first person, past: meeting the headmen I was not rid of anxiety ... now I go nowhere searching
alternatives: the Darpan: a general statement in the present (anxiety from lust and the other foes cannot be removed by headmen ...)
decided because: ਚੁਕਾਇਆ, ਪਤੀਆਇਆ, ਆਇਆ, ਪਾਈ are past and ਜਾਈ is first person; the Faridkot Teeka and the Shabdarth read it as the speaker's own account.

issue: ਘਰਿ ਬੈਠੇ
our reading: sitting at home (literal)
alternatives: the Darpan: settled within, in one's inner self
decided because: the words say sitting at home; the inner sense is not forced into the line, and the Faridkot Teeka keeps it literal.

issue: ਰਾਮਦਾਸ ਸਰੋਵਰੁ
our reading: the pool of Ramdas, with a note (the pool at Amritsar; the shabad also calls it the Sants' pool)
alternatives: the Darpan: the pool of Ram's servants, the Saadh Sangat; the Faridkot Teeka and the Shabdarth: Guru Ram Das's pool at Amritsar
decided because: the name is kept as the line has it; the note gives the pool and the shabad's own link of it with the Sants (line 11) and the Name.

issue: ਸਹੀ ਸਲਾਮਤਿ ਨਾਇ ਆਏ / ਅਪਣਾ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਧਿਆਏ
our reading: (we) have bathed and come back safe and sound, and have meditated on (our) own God
alternatives: the Darpan: whoever meditates on his God bathes and keeps his spiritual capital safe (third person, present)
decided because: ਆਏ and ਧਿਆਏ are plural past forms; the Faridkot Teeka and the Shabdarth read we bathed and came safely.

issue: ਬਾਬਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਰਣਾਈ
our reading: O brother, Nanak (has come) to God's refuge, which has wiped out all worry
alternatives: the Darpan: O Nanak, (say,) O brother, whoever stays in God's refuge is rid of all worry; a published reading: Baba Nanak seeks God's refuge
decided because: ਬਾਬਾ is the vocative O brother, as in the Granth's meanings (107.4) and Sorath (refrains of batch 01); Nanak speaks of himself (§12), and ਮਿਟਾਈ is past, as the Faridkot Teeka reads it.

issue: ਜਪਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਚੁ ਸਾਖੀ
our reading: a command: repeat the Naam, O Nanak: it is the true witness
alternatives: the Faridkot Teeka: I repeat your Name; a published reading: Nanak chants the Naam
decided because: ਜਪਿ beside the vocative ਨਾਨਕ is a command, as the Darpan reads it.

issue: ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਭਇਓ ਸਾਖੀ
our reading: the Guru's Shabad has become manifest
alternatives: the Faridkot Teeka: has become our witness
decided because: the Darpan (ਸਾਖਿਆਤ) and the Shabdarth (ਪਰਗਟ ਹੋਇਆ) both read manifest; in line 17 ਸਾਖੀ, with ਨਾਮੁ ਸਚੁ, is the witness, as the Darpan glosses it there.

issue: ਤਾਪੁ ਛੋਡਿ ਗਇਆ ਪਰਵਾਰੇ
our reading: the fever has left the family (literal)
alternatives: the Darpan: the fever of vices has left the senses (the family)
decided because: the words say fever and family; the Faridkot Teeka and the Shabdarth read it so.

issue: ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਅੰਤਰਜਾਮੀ
our reading: a request: show grace, O Knower of hearts
alternatives: a published reading: the Knower of hearts has granted his mercy
decided because: ਕਰਿ with the vocative ਅੰਤਰਜਾਮੀ is an imperative; the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read it as a prayer.

issue: ਵਡਭਾਗੀ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਪਾਇਆ
our reading: the fortunate have found the True Guru
alternatives: published readings: by great fortune I found the True Guru
decided because: line 10 closes the stanza with ਸੇ ਵਡਭਾਗਾ (those fortunate ones) and plural ਜੀਵਹਿ; the Darpan reads the fortunate ones as the agent.

issue: ਤਾ ਗਤਿ ਭਈ ਹਮਾਰੀ
our reading: then came my liberation
alternatives: the Darpan: then my high spiritual state was formed
decided because: ਗਤਿ alone here is liberation, the high state; the Faridkot Teeka reads ਮੁਕਤੀ; the sense is the same.

review: Doubt decided against the grammar: the rhyme with ਸਵਾਰੇ and the Faridkot/Shabdarth past reading do not outweigh the verb form (ਨਮਸਕਾਰੇ with singular ਗੁਰੁ ਪੂਰਾ = present third person, as ਧਿਆਏ at 624.1 line 14); take the Darpan's general reading, whoever bows to the Perfect Guru, and (his) in lines 2 and 4.

issue: ਗੁਰੁ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਮਸਕਾਰੇ: who bows, and when? (supersedes the writer's doubt, after the review's fix)
our reading: (Whoever) bows to the Perfect Guru: God has set right all (his) affairs and fully upheld (his) honour; the Rahao's servant, and stanza 2 (the pool, Maya following, no shortage) then tell of that one, the Guru speaking in the first person only in ਮੇਰੇ ਪੂਰੇ ਸਤਗੁਰ and stanza 4
alternatives: (I/we) have bowed, a past act of the Guru's own thanksgiving (Faridkot Teeka: ਤੇਰੇ ਚਰਨ ਨਮਸਕਾਰੇ ਹੈਂ ... ਹਮਾਰੇ ਕਾਮ), helped by the rhyme with ਸਵਾਰੇ
decided because: ਨਮਸਕਾਰੇ with the singular object ਗੁਰੁ ਪੂਰਾ is a third-person present like ਧਿਆਏ (624.1 line 14), not a perfect (that would be ਨਮਸਕਾਰਿਆ) nor a first person (ਨਮਸਕਾਰਉ); the Darpan glosses ਸਿਰ ਨਿਵਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ and reads ਜੇਹੜਾ ਮਨੁੱਖ ... ਉਸ ਦੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਕੰਮ ... ਉਸ ਦੀ ਲਾਜ. Lines 1, 2 and 4 now agree in both languages; lines 3 and 5 to 18 need no change, and the pool reading of line 7 stands with it.

issue: ਦਯਿ (line 2), changed by the review from the Merciful Lord to the Master
our reading: the Master (ਮਾਲਕ (ਪ੍ਰਭੂ))
alternatives: the beloved Lord (Darpan here: ਪਿਆਰ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੇ); the Inspirer, God (Faridkot: ਪ੍ਰੇਰਕ ਪਰਮੇਸਰ)
decided because: The Darpan itself glosses ਦਯਿ as ਖਸਮ ਨੇ at Ang 302 to 315, the Granth's meanings render it the Master there, and the sense (God as the instrumental agent) is the same; kept for consistency.

issue: Who made the fallen pure and gave the Lord's praise (ਕਰਿ ਲੀਨੇ … ਦੀਨੇ, no agent named)?
our reading: (the Sants) of line 8 have made the fallen pure and in grace given them the Lord's praise
alternatives: God (Bhai Manmohan Singh: the Lord made me, a sinner, pure); unspecified (Faridkot: we sinners were made pure)
decided because: Line 8 names the Sants just before, and the plural ਲੀਨੇ / ਦੀਨੇ fits them; the Darpan reads it so; God enters only in line 11 (ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ਕਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਪਾਲਾ).

issue: ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਰਣੀ ਪਾਇਆ: Nanak the subject or a vocative?
our reading: O Nanak, (he) has found peace in (God's) refuge
alternatives: Nanak has found peace in the refuge (refuge rule of style §12)
decided because: Lines 15 to 17 tell of the one to whom the Creator gives the gift, and ਪਾਇਆ continues that subject (Jam's servant has not come near him); the Darpan reads Nanak as vocative.

issue: ਖੇਮ ਕੁਸਲ ਭਇਆ ਇਸਨਾਨਾ
our reading: the bathing has taken place in peace and well-being
alternatives: the peace and joy that came is itself the bath (Darpan); I bathe with joy (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: The words name the bathing and peace together; the Faridkot Teeka reads it so (ਸੁਖ ਅਨੰਦ ਸਾਥ ਇਸਨਾਨ ਭਇਆ), and it fits line 9's bathing in the pool; it keeps the line's own subject, ਇਸਨਾਨਾ.

issue: ਗੁਰ ਗੋਪਾਲ: the great Gopal, or the Guru who is Gopal?
our reading: the great Gopal is bliss itself
alternatives: the Guru, Gopal, is blissful (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh); united with the Guru one gets Gopal's bliss (Faridkot)
decided because: The Darpan reads ਗੁਰ as great here, and the Granth's meanings render ਗੁਰ ਗੋਪਾਲਿ / ਗੁਰ ਗੋਪਾਲਾ so at 382.1 and 453.2; line 16 goes on with the Lord of supreme bliss, not the Guru.

issue: ਰਾਮਦਾਸਿ ਸਰੋਵਰ: the pool at Amritsar, or the pool of the Lord's servants (the Saadh Sangat)?
our reading: the pool of Ramdas, with a note giving both senses
alternatives: Darpan: only the Saadh Sangat; Faridkot, the Shabdarth, Sant Singh Khalsa: Guru Ram Das's pool at Amritsar
decided because: The words name the pool of Ramdas; both readings are traditional, so the line keeps the name and the note gives the two senses without choosing for the reader.

issue: Speaker of the opening stanza
our reading: the soul-bride speaks in the first person (frightens (me), (my) bed, (my) Husband)
alternatives: the Darpan tells it in the third person of a wife whose husband is away
decided because: The Rahao (ਹੁਣਿ ਨਹੀ ਸੰਦੇਸਰੋ ਮਾਇਓ) and stanza 2 (ਨਿਹਾਰਉ, first person) are the bride's own words to her mother; the Shabdarth reads the stanza in the first person too.

issue: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਸੁਖਿ ਵਸੰਤੀ: vocative or subject?
our reading: servant Nanak dwells in peace
alternatives: O servant Nanak, (that person) lives in bliss (Darpan)
decided because: Nanak speaks of himself in the first stanza (ਕਰਮੁ ਨ ਜਾਣਾ, ਨਾਮੁ ਪਰਿਓ ਭਗਤੁ), and the Faridkot Teeka, the Shabdarth and both English translations read Nanak as the one who dwells in peace.

issue: ਬਖਸਿ ਲਏ … ਪਾਵੈ: statement or prayer?
our reading: a statement: God forgives past failings and sets one on the path
alternatives: a request, Please forgive (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: ਲਏ and ਪਾਵੈ are third-person indicatives completing the father's simile of lines 6 and 7; the Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka and the Shabdarth read them so.

issue: ਗੁਰੁ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਮਸਕਾਰੇ: who bows, and when?
our reading: (I) have bowed to the Perfect Guru
alternatives: whoever bows to the Perfect Guru (Darpan, present, general)
decided because: The shabad is the Guru's own thanksgiving (ਮੇਰੇ ਪੂਰੇ ਸਤਗੁਰ, ਸੁਆਮੀ ਮੋਰਾ), ਨਮਸਕਾਰੇ rhymes with the perfect ਸਵਾਰੇ, and the Faridkot Teeka and the Shabdarth read a past act.

issue: ਤਾਲੁ ਦਿਵਾਇਆ
our reading: the Creator has had the pool made
alternatives: the Creator gave (through the Guru) the hidden treasure of the Naam, ਤਾਲੁ as a lock (Darpan)
decided because: ਤਾਲੁ is a pool or tank (Sanskrit tala, Punjabi ਤਾਲ); the Faridkot Teeka, the Shabdarth and both English translations read the pool, and the next shabad (625.3) is on bathing in the pool of Ramdas.

issue: ਸਭਿ ਜੀਅ ਭਏ ਕਿਰਪਾਲਾ
our reading: all beings have become kind
alternatives: all who remember become the image of the Merciful One (Darpan); all have become kind to me (Shabdarth, Sant Singh Khalsa)
decided because: The plain words say all beings have become kind; the meaning keeps that without adding to whom, as in 626.1 line 8.

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭਿ ਅਪਨੇ ਕਰਿ ਦੀਨੇ: whose own?
our reading: God has made (them) his own
alternatives: God has made them my friends (Faridkot, Shabdarth, Sant Singh Khalsa)
decided because: The reflexive ਅਪਨੇ refers to the agent, ਪ੍ਰਭਿ; the Darpan reads it so.

issue: ਸਗਲ ਜੀਅ ਵਸਿ ਕੀਨੇ: under whose sway?
our reading: God has brought all beings under (his) sway
alternatives: has made all beings subject to me (Faridkot, Shabdarth, Sant Singh Khalsa)
decided because: The agent of the sentence is God (line 7, ਪ੍ਰਭਿ ਅਪਨੈ) and the line names no one else; the Darpan reads it so, and it matches 626.1 line 8.

issue: ਮਨਿ ਤਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਿ ਸਮਾਵੈ: the Darpan gives ਸਮਾਵੈ and ਗਾਵੈ a generic subject (the person whose past merit has sprung up); the review made servant Nanak the subject of both, rendering ਸਮਾਵੈ as a participle (staying absorbed).
our reading: Staying absorbed, in mind and body, in the sight of the Lord, servant Nanak sings the praises of the True One.
alternatives: Darpan: that person stays absorbed in the Lord's sight and sings his praises (O servant Nanak, say). Faridkot: the servant who sings the praises, his mind and body merge in the Lord's sight.
decided because: ਸਮਾਵੈ and ਗਾਵੈ are both 3rd singular with no relative word, and ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸ is their only named subject, consistent with the speaker the writer reads in the Rahao; the participle keeps both actions of the one subject without an antecedent-less he.

issue: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਸਾਚੁ ਸੁਭਾਖਿਆ: Darpan reads ਹੇ ਦਾਸ ਨਾਨਕ! (ਆਖ) I utter the Name.
our reading: Servant Nanak has uttered (the Name of) the True One.
alternatives: O servant Nanak, (say) …; Nanak has spoken the truth.
decided because: Nanak speaks of himself (style §12); ਸੁਭਾਖਿਆ is perfect, so past kept.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸ: Darpan reads ਦਾਸ as plural (your servants abide in your refuge), Nanak vocative.
our reading: Servant Nanak is in your refuge.
alternatives: O Nanak, your servants are in your refuge.
decided because: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸ is the compound 'servant Nanak', as the Granth's meanings render it (200.2, 193.4).

issue: Rahao: Darpan generic (whoever met the Saadh Sangat); Faridkot and the line's ਹਮਾਰਾ point to the speaker.
our reading: (I) have meditated … have found the fruit.
alternatives: (Whoever) has meditated … has found the fruit.
decided because: Line 2's ਸਭੁ ਕਾਜੁ ਹਮਾਰਾ and the Faridkot Teeka read the speaker; lines 3-4 stay general as their ਜਾ ਕੇ requires.

issue: ਮੰਦਾ ਕੋ ਨ ਅਲਾਏ / ਸਭ ਜੈ ਜੈ ਕਾਰੁ ਸੁਣਾਏ: Darpan makes the devotee the subject (he speaks no evil, tells all of God's praise).
our reading: No one speaks ill (of him); all the world acclaims (him).
alternatives: He speaks no ill word and proclaims God's praise to all (Darpan).
decided because: ਕੋ (anyone) as subject is the plain reading, with the Faridkot Teeka; the Rahao's theme is the protection of the Master's refuge.

issue: ਅਨਦ ਕਰਹੁ ਪਿਤ ਮਾਤਾ: 2nd plural imperative (Rejoice, father and mother) or 3rd plural hortative (let them rejoice).
our reading: Let father and mother rejoice.
alternatives: Rejoice, O father and mother.
decided because: The Darpan's grammar note gives ਕਰਹੁ here as ਹੁਕਮੀ ਭਵਿਖਤ, ਅੱਨ ਪੁਰਖ, ਬਹੁ-ਵਚਨ; the parents are spoken of, not addressed.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਸਰਣੀ ਆਇਆ: Darpan generic (whoever comes to the refuge obtains).
our reading: Nanak has come to (his) refuge and has found the fruit.
alternatives: O Nanak, whoever comes to his refuge obtains the fruit.
decided because: No relative word in the line; Nanak is the plain subject (§12).

issue: ਸਦਾ ਸਦਾ ਹਰਿ ਜਾਪੇ: Darpan imperative (ਜਾਪਿ); Faridkot and the published translations first person.
our reading: Repeat (the Name of) the Lord for ever and ever.
alternatives: I ever repeat the Lord's Name.
decided because: ਜਾਪੇ is not a first-person form (that would be ਜਾਪਉ); the Darpan reads ਜਾਪਿ, and line 2 then states a general truth (God is the protector of children).

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਬਾਲਕ ਰਾਖੇ ਆਪੇ: 'God himself is the protector of children' (Darpan, Faridkot) or 'God has saved my child'.
our reading: God himself is the protector of children.
alternatives: God himself has saved the child.
decided because: ਪ੍ਰਭ has no sihari, so it is not an agent of a perfect verb; ਰਾਖੇ is the noun 'protector' (Darpan, Faridkot).

issue: Darpan generic (whoever meditates on his Guru settles in the heart); Faridkot first person plural.
our reading: Meditating on our own Guru, (and) meeting (him), (we) have come home safe and well.
alternatives: Whoever meditates on his Guru dwells within his own heart in bliss.
decided because: ਆਏ is plural, as the Faridkot Teeka's ਹਮ; ਘਰਿ ਆਏ is taken in its plain sense.

issue: ਬੰਨਾ: barrier (Darpan) or support (Faridkot).
our reading: The Supreme God has raised a dam (against misfortune).
alternatives: The Supreme God has given his support.
decided because: ਬੰਨਾ is an embankment that holds back; line 2 (breaking the camp of pain) follows from it.

issue: ਤਿਨਿ: the Bani (it) or the person in whom it dwells (Darpan).
our reading: it has wiped away all anxiety.
alternatives: he (in whom the Bani came to dwell) has rid himself of all anxiety.
decided because: The line before names no person; ਤਿਨਿ points back to the Bani.

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ: vocative (no sihari) or nominative.
our reading: God, the True Guru, merciful to the meek (nominative).
alternatives: O God, O True Guru …
decided because: Lines 1 and 3 are third person (ਰਾਖੇ, not ਰਾਖਹਿ); Darpan and Faridkot read it nominative.

issue: ਢੋਆ: gift (Darpan), union (Faridkot), support (translations).
our reading: true is the gift of the True One.
alternatives: True is the support of the True One.
decided because: ਢੋਆ is an offering or gift (Darpan's ਤੋਹਫ਼ਾ, ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਸ਼).

issue: Stanza 2: Darpan generic; Faridkot first person.
our reading: (I) have sung (his) praise … (I) have erased self-conceit.
alternatives: (Whoever) has sung … has erased self-conceit.
decided because: Stanza 1 is first person (ਹਮਾਰੀ), and the Faridkot Teeka reads stanza 2 so.

issue: Darpan generic plural (those who worshipped the Guru); Faridkot first person.
our reading: Worshipping the perfect Guru, (I) have accomplished all (my) tasks.
alternatives: Those who worshipped the perfect Guru accomplished all their tasks.
decided because: The Rahao (ਰਾਮੁ ਜਪਤ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ) is the speaker's own peace, as the Faridkot Teeka reads it.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸਿ ਵਖਾਣੀ: Darpan 'O Nanak, (some rare) servant has uttered'.
our reading: Servant Nanak has uttered it.
alternatives: O Nanak, (only a rare) servant has uttered it.
decided because: ਦਾਸਿ is the agent and ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸਿ is 'servant Nanak' (as our word list gives it).

review: Doubt on line 2 decided wrongly. That ਤੀਰਥ ਸੇਵਨ is the ordinary phrase does not settle it. The context does: the Ninth Guru calls tiraths fruitless (830.4, 831.1, 1428.17), and his next shabad repeats the line with ਗੁਰ ਜਨੁ (631.5). So this line lists the holy as the ones not served. The Darpan's reading is applied in the fixes above.

issue: Who has come home: the line names no subject.
our reading: (I) have come home in peace and well-being.
alternatives: Darpan: the one the Guru honours settles, spiritually whole, in the heart-home (third person, ਘਰਿ = the heart).
decided because: ਆਇਆ masculine singular with no subject; the Faridkot Teeka (ਹਮਾਰਾ … ਆਵਣਾ) and the shabad's own first-person tone (ਪਹਿਰਾਇਆ, ਬਿਨਸੇ ਦੁਖ) favour the speaker; the plain ਘਰ is kept, the spiritual sense left to the reader.

issue: ਆਗੈ … ਪਾਛੇ: ahead and behind.
our reading: the world to come (ਆਗੈ) and this world (ਪਾਛੇ).
alternatives: Darpan: the life ahead and the time gone by.
decided because: The glossary's ਆਗੈ = ਪਰਲੋਕ ਵਿੱਚ and the Faridkot Teeka read the pair as hereafter and here, the common Gurbani sense; ਅੱਗੇ / ਪਿੱਛੇ kept with the gloss in brackets.

issue: ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਸਚੁ ਸਾਖੈ: statement (the teaching is true) or cause.
our reading: (this is) owing to the True Guru's teaching of the Truth (ਸਚੁ, the True One, a noun).
alternatives: The teaching of the True Guru is true (Manmohan Singh); by taking the Guru's true teaching (Faridkot).
decided because: ਸਚੁ is masculine with aunkar and cannot qualify feminine ਸਾਖੈ as an adjective; it names the True One taught; the line closes the stanza as the ground of God's protection (Darpan, Faridkot).

issue: ਤੁਮੑ ਧਿਆਈ: indicative or wish.
our reading: I meditate on you at all hours (indicative).
alternatives: Darpan: may I meditate on you (subjunctive).
decided because: The stanza is a run of statements (your shelter, you are powerful); the Faridkot Teeka reads ਧ੍ਯਾਵਤਾ ਹੂੰ.

issue: ਸਤਿਗੁਰ (no sihari) with ਦੀਆ: vocative or agent.
our reading: O True Guru, those you have comforted …
alternatives: The True Guru has given comfort (Faridkot, the translators).
decided because: ਸਤਿਗੁਰ without sihari is the vocative form (the agent would be ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ); the Darpan reads ਹੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ; line 8's plural ਆਏ makes the comforted plural.

issue: Who meditated and whose face is bright.
our reading: Nanak has meditated on the Naam, and (his) face is radiant.
alternatives: Darpan: O Nanak, those who meditated became radiant-faced (plural).
decided because: ਨਾਨਕ … ਧਿਆਇਆ is an ergative past with Nanak as agent (as the Faridkot Teeka and §12, Nanak speaking of himself); ਮੁਖ … ਭਏ is the plural of the face, honorific.

issue: Whom the Lord saved and who tasted the Name (ਰਾਖੇ, ਚਾਖੇ plural).
our reading: (his servants), who have tasted the Lord's Name.
alternatives: (us): he saved us, we have tasted (Faridkot).
decided because: Either fits the plural; the Darpan's reading keeps lines 3–4 one clause about those saved.

issue: ਜੀਅ ਹੋਏ ਮਿਹਰਵਾਨ.
our reading: (all) beings have become merciful (to me): ਜੀਅ the subject.
alternatives: Darpan: God has become merciful to all beings (ਜੀਅ oblique).
decided because: ਜੀਅ stands without a postposition before ਹੋਏ, the plain subject; the Faridkot Teeka and Manmohan Singh read it so, and it matches 631.2's honour everywhere.

issue: ਤੀਰਥ ਸੇਵੇ.
our reading: served at the places of pilgrimage.
alternatives: Darpan: ਤੀਰਥ = holy persons (ਸੰਤ ਜਨ), citing 631.5's ਗੁਰ ਜਨੁ ਸੇਵਿਓ.
decided because: ਤੀਰਥ ਸੇਵਨ is the ordinary phrase for frequenting tiraths, and the Faridkot Teeka and Manmohan Singh read it so; the line lists what the man failed to do, not a teaching.

issue: ਗੁਰ ਜਨੁ.
our reading: the Guru (ਗੁਰ ਜਨੁ, the Guru as a person).
alternatives: the Guru and his servants (Sant Singh Khalsa); a great soul (Faridkot, ਮਹਾਪੁਰਸ਼).
decided because: ਜਨੁ is singular; the Darpan and Manmohan Singh take it as the Guru himself.

issue: ਪਾਇ ਪਦ: feet or station.
our reading: Having gained the station (ਪਦ) of the human body, worship the Lord.
alternatives: Worship the Lord's feet (Faridkot, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: ਮਾਨਸ ਦੇਹ ਪਾਇ ਪਦ: ਪਦ follows ਪਾਇ as its object (the Darpan's ਮਾਨਸ ਦੇਹ ਪਦ, the rank of the human body); ਹਰਿ ਭਜੁ is complete without feet.

issue: ਕਉਨੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਗੁਰ.
our reading: Which Name is it, O Guru (ਗੁਰ vocative)?
alternatives: Darpan: which Name taught by the Guru.
decided because: The shabad poses a seeker's questions answered in stanza 2; ਗੁਰ without a postposition reads as the address (Faridkot: ਹੇ ਗੁਰ).

issue: ਨਾਨਕ with ਤੁਮ ਹੀ ਮਹਿ.
our reading: O Nanak, he dwells within you yourself.
alternatives: Says Nanak: (to the listener).
decided because: No verb of saying; ਨਾਨਕ is the vocative signature, as §12 has it when the line tells of another.

issue: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ.
our reading: In me, servant Nanak, there is no virtue (Nanak of himself).
alternatives: Darpan: O servant Nanak, (say)…
decided because: ਮੈ ਨਾਹਿ ਕੋਊ ਗੁਨੁ is the speaker's own confession; §12: Nanak speaking of himself is the subject.

review: Doubt on line 1 (ਭਾਈ to God): the reading is upheld. It is a vocative, not the predicate ਪ੍ਰੇਮੀ settled at 614.1 (ਹਮ ਅਪਰਾਧੀ ਨਿਰਗੁਣੇ ਭਾਈ in line 2 cannot take ਭਾਈ as a predicate); in the lines spoken to God (ਤੂ, ਤੁਝ) the Darpan glosses it ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ and the Faridkot ਹੇ ਭਾਵਨ ਰੂਪ. Only the English wording is wrong (fixed in en lines 1, 2, 4, 9). Doubt on line 0 (ਪਹਿਲਾ unrendered) upheld: ਪਹਿਲਾ is masculine with ਮਹਲਾ, not the feminine ਦੁਤੁਕੀ, and 14.1 (ਮਹਲਾ ਪਹਿਲਾ ੧) already renders it inside 'the First Guru'; no ashtapadi heading in the Granth's meanings renders such a ਪਹਿਲਾ separately. Doubt on line 19 (God, not Maya) upheld, but see the voice fix there.
reviewer_fix: Keep the vocative to God; render it O dear one (pa ਹੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ!) and add the note.

review: Doubt on line 31 overturned: ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ ਮਿਲਿਐ is the absolute (on meeting), and ਕੀਨੀ has no stated agent; the Darpan and the Faridkot both make it the Guru, the writer makes it God; the line is left as it stands (fixed in pa/en). Line 17 made consistent with 636.2. The other doubts of 634.2 (lines 4, 5, 12, 13, 15, 26, 34) are borne out by the grammar and context.
reviewer_fix: Leave the agent of ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕੀਨੀ unstated.

review: Doubt on line 19 overturned (the world, with both commentaries; fixed in pa/en). Doubts on lines 9 and 23 upheld.
reviewer_fix: (the world) weeps, robbed by its faults.

issue: Subject of ਬਸਾਵੈ, ਸਿਰਾਵੈ, ਭਇਓ, ਆਇਓ, ਚੇਤਿਓ in the stanzas.
our reading: The mind (it), the subject of the Rahao, throughout.
alternatives: Darpan, Faridkot: the jiv (a person); Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa: I (stanza 3).
decided because: All the verbs are third person masculine singular, as ਮਨੁ is; the near-identical Gauri shabad 219.6 is already rendered with the mind as it; Nanak in line 8 is the vocative signature (a third-person line, §12).

issue: ਨਿਜ ਮਤੁ ਸਾਧਨ ਕਉ.
our reading: the Saadhs' own counsel (ਕਉ as of).
alternatives: My own view (ਨਿਜ = mine), spoken to the holy.
decided because: The Darpan glosses ਕਉ here as ਦਾ (of) and reads the counsel of the Gurmukhs; ਤੋਹਿ (to you) is the addressee, so ਸਾਧਨ ਕਉ is not a dative.

issue: What is not straightened (ਭਇਓ ਨ ਸੂਧਉ).
our reading: (the mind) has not become straight, like a dog's tail.
alternatives: Darpan: the tail (ਸਿੱਧੀ) is the subject.
decided because: ਭਇਓ and ਸੂਧਉ are masculine, so the subject is ਮਨ (line 5), not the feminine ਪੂਛ; as 536.2 has it.

issue: ਨਾਮੁ ਤੁਹਾਰਉ ਲੀਨਉ: tense.
our reading: I have taken your Name (past).
alternatives: Darpan: (then) I can take your Name.
decided because: ਲੀਨਉ is a past participle; the line pleads by the Name already taken, as the ground of the prayer; Nanak speaks of himself to God, so Says Nanak.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਬਿਰਦੁ ਪਛਾਨਉ: prayer or statement.
our reading: O Lord, keep in mind your age-old way (ਹਰਿ vocative, ਪਛਾਨਉ imperative).
alternatives: I recognise the Lord's age-old way (first person).
decided because: The Darpan reads ਹਰਿ as ਹੇ ਹਰੀ and the line as a plea, which ਭੂਲੇ ਸਦਾ ਪਰਾਨੀ (mortals always err) completes.

issue: Person in the stanzas after a Rahao addressed to the mind.
our reading: Third person, (man): Leaving the True, (man) has clung to the false.
alternatives: Second person, continuing O mind, you…
decided because: Line 6 names the subject in the third person (ਬਉਰਾ, the madman) and line 8 speaks of mortals (ਪਰਾਨੀ); the Darpan reads the stanzas so.

issue: ਸਹਜਿ ਰਤੇ ਮਨ ਭਾਈ.
our reading: it is pleasing to (my) mind, dyed in Sahaj (ਭਾਈ verb).
alternatives: Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa: O brother.
decided because: The Darpan (ਭਾਈ, ਪਸੰਦ ਆ ਗਈ ਹੈ) and the Faridkot Teeka (ਮਨ ਮੇਂ ਤਿਸ ਕੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਤੀ ਭਾਈ) both take it as the verb; the line has no addressee.

issue: ਮਤਿ ਸਾਈ.
our reading: you give understanding, O Master (ਸਾਈ vocative).
alternatives: Faridkot: you give that very understanding (ਸਾਈ, that same).
decided because: The Darpan reads ਸਾਈ as ਹੇ ਸਾਈਂ, and the stanza ends addressing God (ਤੂ … ਤੂ).

issue: ਮਨੂਆ ਪਉਣੁ ਬਿੰਦੁ ਸੁਖਵਾਸੀ ਨਾਮਿ ਵਸੈ ਸੁਖ ਭਾਈ.
our reading: If the mind, restless as the wind, dwells even a little in the Name, the home of peace, there is peace, O brother.
alternatives: ਭਾਈ as pleasing (peace is pleasing).
decided because: The Darpan's ਪਦਅਰਥ gives ਭਾਈ here as ਹੇ ਭਾਈ, and the Faridkot Teeka reads the same.

issue: ਸੋਤ੍ਰ.
our reading: ears.
alternatives: Darpan: the senses (ਇੰਦ੍ਰੇ).
decided because: ਸੋਤ੍ਰ is Skt. śrotra, the ear, listed with tongue and eyes; the Faridkot Teeka and both translators read ears.

issue: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸਹਜਿ ਪੀਆਈ: who gives the Amrit.
our reading: they have been given Amrit to drink (agent left unstated).
alternatives: Darpan: the Guru has made them drink; Faridkot: they make seekers drink.
decided because: ਪੀਆਈ is causative with no agent named; the giver is left as the line leaves it.

issue: ਗੁਰੁ ਦਾਤਾ ਮੇਲੇ.
our reading: If the Guru unites (one) with the Giver.
alternatives: If the Guru, the Giver, unites (one).
decided because: ਗੁਰੁ is the subject (aunkar); the Darpan takes ਦਾਤਾ as the Giver (God) with whom the Guru unites.

issue: Who shows grace on meeting the True Guru.
our reading: (you, God) have shown grace.
alternatives: Darpan: the Guru shows grace; Manmohan Singh: God shows grace to him who meets the Guru.
decided because: The stanza addresses God throughout (ਤੇਰਾ, ਤੁਧੁ, ਤੂ, ਤੁਮਾਰਾ); ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ ਮਿਲਿਐ is the locative absolute, on meeting the Guru, not the agent.

issue: ਸਬਦੁ ਗੁਰ ਪੀਰਾ ਗਹਿਰ ਗੰਭੀਰਾ.
our reading: The Shabad of the Guru, the Pir, is deep and profound.
alternatives: The Shabad is his Guru and Pir (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa); the Darpan: by the Guru-Pir's Shabad he becomes deep.
decided because: ਗੁਰ without ending is the genitive before ਸਬਦੁ's predicate; ਗਹਿਰ ਗੰਭੀਰਾ then describes the Shabad, with no subject supplied.

issue: ਬਕੈ (third person) beside ਕਰਹੁ (second person plural).
our reading: (The pandit) stands and recites …, (but) you do worldly deeds.
alternatives: Darpan: you recite … you do.
decided because: The persons are kept as the verbs give them.

issue: ਪਤਿ ਪਰਵਾਨਾ ਸਾਚ ਕਾ.
our reading: Honour is the pass of the True One (ਪਤਿ = honour).
alternatives: Darpan: ਪਤਿ = the Husband Lord: the Name is the pass to the Lord.
decided because: ਪਤਿ is the ordinary word for honour, and the Faridkot Teeka and both translators read honour; the line then pairs the pass (honour) and its seal (the Naam).

issue: ਅਵਗਣਿ ਮੁਠੀ ਰੋਇ: who weeps (feminine).
our reading: (the soul-bride), robbed by her faults, weeps.
alternatives: Darpan: the world's people (ਲੋਕਾਈ).
decided because: ਮੁਠੀ is feminine singular; the soul-bride is Gurbani's usual feminine subject of such lines; the sense is the same.

issue: ਨਾਉ ਮਿਲੈ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆਂ … ਮਿਲਾਉ.
our reading: May I gain the Name and be content; may I be united (first-person wish).
alternatives: Faridkot: the content gain the Name, and the Gracious One unites them.
decided because: ਮਿਲਾਉ is first person singular (subjunctive), following ਹਉ … ਜਾਉ of line 22; the Darpan reads ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆਂ as I would be content.

issue: ਪਹਿਲਾ in ਸੋਰਠਿ ਮਹਲਾ ੧ ਪਹਿਲਾ ਦੁਤੁਕੀ.
our reading: Not rendered separately: it repeats ਮਹਲਾ ੧ (the First Guru).
alternatives: The first Dutuki.
decided because: Only one Dutuki stands here; ਪਹਿਲਾ agrees with ਮਹਲਾ (masculine), not with the feminine ਦੁਤੁਕੀ.

issue: ਭਾਈ in a line addressed to God (lines 1, 2, 4, 9).
our reading: my Beloved (ਹੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ!).
alternatives: O brother (the translators).
decided because: These lines speak to God (ਤੂ, ਤੁਝ); the Darpan glosses ਭਾਈ in the Rahao as ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ and the Faridkot Teeka as ਹੇ ਭਾਵਨ ਰੂਪ (O dear one); in the other lines no one else is in view, and O brother is kept.

issue: ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਆਖੈ ਆਪਣਾ: what everyone calls his own.
our reading: Everyone calls (God) his own; the All-wise One is understood through the Guru.
alternatives: Darpan: everyone speaks of (Maya) as his own; the one who understands from the Guru becomes wise.
decided because: The Faridkot Teeka and both translators read God; ਸੁਜਾਨੁ then names God as known through the Guru.

review: Doubt on line 6 (ਪੈਜ ਰਖੁ) decided wrongly. The grammar does not allow a statement: ਰਖੁ is the imperative, set against ਰਖਦਾ (line 2) in the same shabad, and the stanzas' list of God's past acts is the ground for the request, not a reason to turn it into a statement. Take the Darpan's request; line 5 becomes its own sentence (fixes above).

Doubt on line 5 (ਦੀਜੈ) decided wrongly: the precative is a request to the Master at whose door the speaker has fallen, as both the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read and as our Granth meanings render ਦੀਜੈ in prayers (100.1, 133.1, 169.2). Fixes above.

issue: line 5 ਏਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ: what does this refer to, with line 6 read as a request?
our reading: (keeping the devotees' honour) is your greatness; line 6 the request (ਰਖੁ imperative), as the review fixed
alternatives: Faridkot reads line 6 as a statement introduced by line 5 (this is your greatness: you keep the honour)
decided because: ਰਖੁ is the imperative (against ਰਖਦਾ in line 2), and the Darpan reads the request with the devotees' honour as God's own honour; the parenthesis keeps both lines' sense without making ਰਖੁ a statement

issue: ਪੈਜ ਰਖੁ: a request (keep the honour) or a statement following ਏਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ (this is your greatness: you keep the honour)?
our reading: statement: this is your greatness, that you keep the honour of your devotees
alternatives: Darpan: a request, ਤੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਭਗਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਇੱਜ਼ਤ ਰੱਖ; Faridkot, Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa: a statement
decided because: the Rahao's first line (this is your greatness) needs its content, and the stanzas list God's acts in protecting devotees (ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ, ਰਾਖਿ ਲਏ); a verb in a list of God's acts is a statement

issue: ਪ੍ਰਹਿਲਾਦ ਜਨ … ਰਾਖਿ ਲਏ: Prahlad alone (honorific plural) or Prahlad and servants like him?
our reading: your servant Prahlad
alternatives: Darpan: Prahlad and many such servants
decided because: ਜਨ stands in apposition to the name, and ਲਏ is the respectful plural, as the Faridkot Teeka reads (ਦਾਸ ਪ੍ਰਹਿਲਾਦ ਜੀ)

issue: ਤੇਰੀ goes with ਮਾਇਆ or with ਲੋਕ (the whole world is yours)?
our reading: the whole world is in attachment to your Maya
alternatives: Darpan: Maya's attachment too is your creation; Manmohan Singh: all those engrossed in Maya are yours
decided because: ਤੇਰੀ is feminine and agrees with ਮਾਇਆ, not with ਲੋਕ (masculine); the Faridkot Teeka reads the same

issue: ਸਚੁ ਬਾਣੀ ਸਚੁ ਸਬਦੁ: the Bani is true, or the True One, the Bani and the Shabad?
our reading: the True One (the Name), the Bani and the Shabad come by the Guru's grace
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh: the true Bani and the true Shabad
decided because: ਸਚੁ with aunkar is a masculine noun and cannot qualify the feminine ਬਾਣੀ; the Darpan reads it as the ever-true Name

issue: ਤੂ ਆਪੇ ਰੰਗੁ ਚੜਾਇ: statement or request?
our reading: statement: you yourself dye (the soul) in your love
alternatives: a request: dye (me) yourself
decided because: the Darpan and Sant Singh Khalsa read a statement, and the Rahao's second line turns to the listeners with the command; ਚੜਾਇ with ਤੂ is read as the present

issue: ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਕਾਰ ਕਮਾਵਣੀ: the one (soul-bride) who does the Guru's work, or the Guru's work is to be done?
our reading: she who does the Guru's work (the soul-bride of stanzas 1 and 3), as line 8 (ਮਨਹਠਿ ਕਾਰ ਕਮਾਵਣੀ) describes her opposite
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa: a command, work to serve the Guru
decided because: the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read the doer; the parallel line 8 describes the unworthy wife the same way

issue: ਸੋ ਜੀਅੜਾ ਜਲਿ ਜਾਉ: a curse (may it burn) or a statement (it burns)?
our reading: may that wretched soul burn
alternatives: Darpan: the soul burns (in vices), glossing ਜਾਉ as ਜਾਇ
decided because: ਜਾਉ is the third-person imperative form, as the Faridkot Teeka reads (ਜਲ ਜਾਵੇ)

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਤਿਸੁ ਸਰਣਾਗਤੀ: Nanak has come to his refuge, or a command to the listener to seek it?
our reading: Nanak (has come to) the refuge of him who cuts away sins
alternatives: Darpan: O Nanak, (say:) O brother, seek the refuge of that God
decided because: no imperative verb stands in the line; the stanza speaks in the first person (ਪੇਖਉ, carried across), and the Faridkot Teeka reads the same

issue: ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਮਿਲਾਇਆ: who is united, and with whom?
our reading: in the Saadh's company (God) has united (me with himself), the One who fills all
alternatives: Darpan: whom God unites in the Guru's company sees him everywhere; Faridkot: the Saadh's company has united me with him
decided because: the stanza is in the first person (ਪੇਖਉ), and ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ (sihari) is the place where the uniting happens

issue: Whom does ਪਿਆਰੇ address?
our reading: God in the Rahao and in lines 15 and 30, whose verbs are second person (ਆਵਹਿ, ਲੈਹਿ); elsewhere the listener (O dear one)
alternatives: Faridkot: God throughout; Sant Singh Khalsa: O Beloved throughout
decided because: many lines speak of God in the third person (ਆਪਿ, ਭੁਲਾਇਅਨੁ, ਮਿਲਾਇਓਨੁ), so their ਪਿਆਰੇ cannot be God; as the Darpan reads; a note says so

issue: ਸੋੁ (read ਸੁ) ਮੁਹਿ ਕਾਲੈ ਉਠਿ ਜਾਇ: who departs with a blackened face, the Saakat or the one who keeps his company?
our reading: such a one (left open as the line leaves it)
alternatives: Darpan: the one who keeps the Saakat's company
decided because: ਸੁ refers back to the line before without naming; 'such a one' keeps the line's own scope

issue: ਮੈ ਕੀਏ ਕਰਮ ਅਨੇਕਾ: I have done many rites, or (people) have done many rites before my eyes?
our reading: I have done many (such) deeds
alternatives: Darpan: before my eyes people do many rites
decided because: ਮੈ ਕੀਏ is the plain ergative, by me were done; the next line goes on in the first person (ਹਾਰਿ ਪਰਿਓ), as the Faridkot Teeka and Sant Singh Khalsa read

issue: ਦੀਜੈ: addressed to whom?
our reading: may (I) be given an intellect that discerns (the precative kept)
alternatives: Faridkot: O Master, give me; Darpan: (praying) O Lord, give me
decided because: the line speaks of the Master in the third person (ਸੁਆਮੀ ਕੈ ਦੁਆਰੈ), so the polite precative is kept without naming an addressee
